beats.speaker: narration
beats.text: Months on. The partnership papers are ready to sign — Dave's booked one more session first.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "I want all three cards out on the table again — the Fool, the Lovers, the Empress — before I sign tomorrow."

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You set the Fool down first.

options.text: One cycle just ended, right as the next one begins.
Something you're nurturing is finally ready to be born.
This is a choice worth weighing from every angle.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "My old coworkers still think I lost it, quitting like that."

options.text: It's fine going against convention — that's the whole card.
It's about holding two sides of yourself in balance.
It's about pleasure and beauty being part of the message.

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You set the Lovers down next.

options.text: Two real paths — the hard part was ever choosing at all.
It's about trusting the path shows up once you take the step.
It's about raw, unformed chaos that hasn't settled yet.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "How do I know signing with him is actually the right call, not just the easy one?"

options.text: Let more than logic decide — body, mind, and spirit all get a vote.
It's about staying calm right at the edge of the fall.
It's about abundance growing in every direction at once.

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: You set the Empress down last.

options.text: Nourish, protect, and grow whatever you're tending.
It's about saying yes to the unknown instead of playing safe.
It's about a real choice you have to weigh carefully.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Some days it still feels like I forced all of this to happen faster than it should have."

options.text: Real abundance comes from allowing things to flourish, not forcing them.
It's about a beginner's mind, curious instead of jaded.
It's about choosing with your gut, not just your head.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Wait — if the Empress is about not forcing things, wasn't quitting my job basically forcing a change?"

options.text: No — that was the Fool's leap, not the Empress's patience. Different card, different moment.
Yes, so the whole reading contradicts itself.
The two cards can't both be true, pick one.

elaboration: Three cards don't have to describe the same moment the same way — the Fool covers the leap itself, the Empress covers what had already been quietly growing underneath it long before you jumped.

beats.speaker: reader
beats.text: All three, together: a leap, a choice, and something patiently grown. That's not a contradiction — that's just what the last year actually was.

beats.speaker: client
beats.text: "Okay. I think I finally see it — a leap, a choice, and something patiently grown, all pulling the same direction. Thank you for laying it all out like that."
